articles.summary: Most small businesses in the Philippines fund a client's job before the client pays for it. A caterer buys ingredients and books servers weeks before the event. A furniture shop orders plywood and hardware before the first cut is made. The full payment usually comes at the end, and for corporate clients, that can mean another 30 to 60 days after the work is delivered. A downpayment is the simplest way to close part of that gap. It moves some of the cost of the work back to the person who asked
articles.title: How to Collect a Downpayment From Clients in the Philippines

In-store QR Ph transactions more than tripled in the same period. For a lot of Philippine businesses the terminal has become optional, and for some it was never worth the rental. articles.title: Do you need a credit card machine? How to accept card payments without a POS terminal in the Philippines

articles.summary: In most hotels, ordering food to your room still runs on a phone call and a printed menu. Someone writes the order down, the kitchen gets a ticket, and the charge is posted to the room to be settled at checkout. That process works, which is probably why few operators look closely at what it costs them. This article looks at where the cost sits, what changes when the menu becomes a QR code the guest scans and pays through, and what to decide before switching. In-room dining or room service? I
articles.title: In-Room Dining: Rethinking Room Service, Orders to Payment

articles.summary: Since launching locally in 2015, New Era PH has become a staple of local street culture. To support their growing online store, they integrated PayMongo for automated settlements and built-in fraud protection. Discover how fintech helps this heritage brand scale securely.
articles.title: New Era PH embracing homegrown communities as a global brand

articles.summary: A Philippine business selling to someone in another country has more ways to get paid than it did ten years ago, and most of them work. Access is no longer the problem. The work now is picking a route that matches how the customer wants to pay, then handling the things that go differently once money crosses a border: who sets the exchange rate, why cards get declined more often, what the fees are, and what happens when a customer in another time zone disputes a charge. articles.title: How to Accept International Payments in the Philippines

articles.summary: Employee reimbursement is how a company pays staff back for business expenses they covered with their own money. A cash advance works the other way around: the company releases the funds first, and the employee accounts for them afterwards in a liquidation report. Both are simple to run when a team is small. As a company grows, employees wait longer to be repaid and finance sees the spending only after the paperwork arrives. This guide covers how reimbursements and cash advances work in the Ph
articles.title: Employee reimbursements and liquidation reports: how to set up a process that holds up

articles.summary: Profit and cash arrive at different times. Profit is recorded when you make the sale. Cash shows up later, after the stock has been bought, the customer's credit term has run out and the payment has cleared. That is how a business can report a good month and still struggle to make payroll on the 15th. It is a common worry. In research by Visa, 44% of small and medium businesses named cash flow as a top issue. This guide explains why the gap opens even in a healthy business, then shows how to me
articles.title: How long does your money take to come back? Why profitable businesses still run short on cash

articles.summary: If you accept cards, you've probably noticed that the payout never matches the sale. A ₱1,000 card payment on our standard rate lands in your balance as ₱950. Where the other ₱50 goes isn't a secret, but almost nobody explains it in a way that helps you decide what to do about it. So this is our attempt.
